summary: The Kitchen page lists the 16 kitchen products. The list is complete and every product has a picture and a price, but the page opens with a 242 px shelf picture and an intro before the first product, the sort menu does nothing without scripts, and on a phone the three-column table shrinks to unreadable size. Most important: a product grid that starts in the first screen and works on phones.
audience: Visitors looking for kitchenware, comparing products and prices.

purpose.clear.evidence: Breadcrumb, the shelf picture and the heading „Kitchen“ make the page clear at once.

purpose.tasks.evidence: All 16 products can be opened, but sorting („Sort by: Most popular“) has no effect and there are no filters by colour or price.

content.complete.evidence: Name, colour, price and a picture for every product.

content.current.evidence: Product data looks current, but the sidebar news and the footer are from 2011.

content.duplicate.evidence: Colour versions are separate products: „Enamel Stove-Top Kettle (Cream)“, „(Sage)“ and „(Red)“ fill three of 16 cards with the same item.

structure.scannable.evidence: A long table of 16 cards with no grouping; the first products start below the picture and intro.

action.primary.evidence: Opening a product is the clear action; each card links name and picture.

nav.menu.evidence: Seven green tabs (Home … Sale!) plus a second department list in the sidebar; the current tab is marked yellow, but Delivery, Returns and Contact live only in the footer.

visual.brand.evidence: The green house-and-leaf logo with the italic Millbrook wordmark, dark green #2f5420 / #4c7f2f and cream surfaces: recognisable on every page and fitting for a home and garden shop. Verdana 11 px is just old, not brand.

visual.images.evidence: The shelf picture and the product photos are sharp and on topic.

visual.hierarchy.evidence: Red prices, „NEW!“ badges and grey „Buy“ buttons are louder than the product names.

visual.consistency.evidence: Same frame, nav, sidebar boxes and footer as the other pages.

trust.signals.evidence: The footer names the shop and its street address; there are no reviews, no returns promise near the products and the payment logos are plain text boxes.

inventory.why: A slim category header with the picture, so products start sooner.
Sorting and colour filter that work.
One card per product with colour swatches instead of one card per colour.

keep: All 16 products with names and prices

fix.text: No viewport: the grid shrinks to unreadable size on phones
Colour versions repeat the same product

design_input: Slim category header with picture and intro
Product grid: 2 columns on phones, 4 on desktop, one card per product with colour swatches
The trust strip from the home page
